title: What can an average hobby time tell us about every child?
description: A line graph shows the average daily time rural and urban children spend on hobbies and games at each age. The video reads a value at age ten, reads an age from a value, tests whether one reading is twice another, and shows why an average cannot speak for every child.
teaching_notes: One idea: a value on this graph is an average, so it can be read in two directions and compared, but it says nothing about every single child. Watch for students who read an average as a rule for all children.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 11)
video_script.why: The child can read a dot and test a doubling, and now meets a graph whose heights are averages.
video_script.substitution: Read a value from an age, read an age from a value, test whether one reading is twice another, and remember that an average describes the group, not each child.
video_script.anchor: the book's line graph of the average daily time children spend on hobbies and games, by age
video_script.payoff_line: it cannot be concluded, because the graph shows an average

final_answer.value: Read from the graph; (b) cannot be concluded because it is an average
final_answer.spoken: the readings come from the graph, and the second statement cannot be concluded, because the graph shows an average

never_show: all rural kids aged 15 spend at least 1 hour
maths_rules: (i) find age 10 on the bottom axis, go up to the urban line and read across to the side scale
(ii) find 1.5 hours on the side scale, go across to the rural line and read the age below it; choose from 8, 10, 12, 14 and 18 years
(iii)(a) divide the age 15 reading by the age 10 reading; the statement holds only if the answer is about 2
(iii)(b) the graph gives an average, so it says nothing about every child; not correct
slip: an average describes the group, not each child in it
video_script.design: One idea: read the graph in both directions, then remember the heights are averages. The graph stays on screen all video; no values are invented.
open_questions: The graph values are not in the extracted book text, so (i), (ii) and (iii)(a) cannot be checked; the video gives the method, and only (iii)(b) is concluded.
